clue.text: Yard in a favela, say – refuge for debtors

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so the yard letter goes inside the slum phrase

blocks.note: a favela is a Brazilian shanty town, an example of a slum; 'a' is kept
Y is the standard abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A yard in a Brazilian shanty town is pictured as a hiding place for people fleeing their creditors.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes in after the S of A SLUM to give ASYLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a sanctuary, and debtors once sought shelter from arrest in such protected places.

clue.text: Reportedly snatch fleece for abrasive stripper?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word for snatch is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to snatch is to steal
a fleece is a sheep's wool

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a sheep's fleece to use for stripping something.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel wool is a pad of fine steel strands used to scour and strip paint or varnish.

clue.text: Body of water to leak out with rain, accommodating duck

indicators.note: out suggests disorder, so the letters are taken out of their order
accommodating means housing, so the letters take the duck in

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
taken as written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Rain leaking out of a lake that a duck is swimming in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Ontario is one of North America's Great Lakes, a body of water.

clue.text: Food for mind in article supporting German writer

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it, so the article comes after the writer

blocks.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article supports a German writer with food for thought.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the article underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the food from heaven in Exodus, and figuratively means spiritual or intellectual nourishment.

clue.text: English used in passage with three lines in correspondence

indicators.note: something used in a set of items is placed among them, so the English letter goes among the lines

blocks.note: PARA is short for paragraph, a passage of writing
L is the abbreviation for line, taken three times
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English passage is used alongside three lines in an exchange of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits between the second and third L. 'Correspondence' looks like letter-writing but means a likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A parallel is a similarity or match between two things, which is correspondence in the sense of agreement.

clue.text: Lively beer reservist drained

indicators.note: drained means emptied of contents, so only the outside letters stay

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A lively army reservist has drained his beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert means quick and wide awake, so lively in the sense of sharp and attentive.

clue.text: I'm going to pass on gold rings

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the gold goes all round

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: A dying person bequeaths gold rings before departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like a noun, jewellery to pass on, but it is a verb meaning encircles.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a farewell said on leaving, so it stands for the announcement 'I'm going'.

clue.text: Boy stopped by Irish landowner

indicators.note: a thing stopped by something is plugged by it, so the second piece fills the first

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A boy is stopped by an Irish landowner on his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner, so the Irish word is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the owner of a landed estate in Scotland, a landowner.

clue.text: Legendary cycle given rewrite tortured Mahler

indicators.note: something given a rewrite has its text reworked, so these letters are set down in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A song cycle gets reworked by a tormented Gustav Mahler, who did write song cycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycle' suggests Mahler's song cycles, but here it is a cycle of legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Morte d'Arthur is Thomas Malory's compilation of Arthurian romances, the classic cycle of legends about King Arthur.

clue.text: Signal stream working

blocks.note: a beck is a northern English word for a brook
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A working stream is somehow signalling, as if water could gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to gesture to someone to come nearer, a kind of signal, used here as a verb.

clue.text: Iron Lady back to join Little Women's cause

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the title for a lady is read from the end

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
mini means small or little
Ms is the title used for a woman

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, returns to join the Little Women in their cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' reads as Margaret Thatcher, but the two words are separate pieces, and the lady's title goes on the end. Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel of four sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminism is the movement advocating women's rights and equality, so it is women's cause.

clue.text: Old-hat Bond somehow less than sensational

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters reach their result by some unstated rearrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange
under a figure means less than it

explanation.surface: A dated James Bond film is judged somehow less than sensational.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes melodramatic, violent entertainment, so it means sensational in the lurid sense.

clue.text: See 9
Horse dispenses with one grey wader

indicators.note: to dispense with something is to do without it, so the letter for one is dropped

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A horse ignores a single grey bird wading nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like the animal but is drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey heron is a common long-legged wading bird of Europe.

clue.text: Astrologer savvy about game over before noon

indicators.note: over in a down clue means turned upside down, so the game word reads upwards
about means surrounding, so the savvy word goes round the rest

blocks.note: nous is common sense or know-how
darts is a pub game
am stands for ante meridiem, before midday

explanation.surface: An astrologer, knowing about the game, predicts it will be over before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was the 16th-century French astrologer famed for his prophecies.

clue.text: Pin inset with silver for rural tenant?

indicators.note: something inset with an item has that item set into it, so the pin word holds the silver

blocks.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge used to fasten parts
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A brooch pin set with silver is offered as something for a country tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager was a farm labourer or villager renting a cottage, a tenant in the countryside.

clue.text: Gallon swallowed by daughter confined to school

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for gallon
swallowed means ate
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter downs a gallon and is kept in school as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowed by' tempts a container, but each word gives its own piece in order. Gated is British school or college slang for being kept within the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be gated is to be forbidden to leave school or college premises as a punishment.

clue.text: Live on the periphery?

blocks.note: re means on, as in concerning
the side of something is its edge or periphery

explanation.surface: Someone is told to live out on the edge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the periphery' reads as one phrase, but 'on' and 'periphery' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to dwell somewhere, a verb synonym of live in its home-making sense.

clue.text: Trouble restarted for British soldier

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so the letters are stirred out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Trouble has started again for a British soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a soldier of the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of the Second World War.

clue.text: Wine there is missing – litres pumped in?

indicators.note: something pumped in is forced inside, so the litres letter goes into the other word

blocks.note: caret is Latin for 'there is lacking', the name of the proofreader's mark for an insertion
L is the abbreviation for litre or litres

explanation.surface: A wine bottle is short, so perhaps more litres were pumped in.
explanation.walkthrough: The caret mark ^ shows where something is missing in a text; its name is Latin for 'there is lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Sea snake Iranian initially placed in US loo

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept
placed in puts the snake and the letter inside the loo word

blocks.note: can is American slang for a toilet
an asp is a venomous snake
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sea snake from Iran is found in an American toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian is the large inland sea bordered by Iran, Russia and others.

clue.text: Barbarians around very French woman after game

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the barbarians enclose the French intensifier

blocks.note: the Huns were nomadic invaders, archetypal barbarians
très is French for very

explanation.surface: Barbarians surround a very French woman who is chasing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After game' looks like following a match; it means pursuing quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntress is a female hunter, a woman who goes after game animals.

clue.text: Lower form runs northern school

blocks.note: secondary means lesser in rank or importance
a mode is a form or manner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A lower form in a northern school goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower form' reads as a junior class; split it. A secondary modern was a British state school for pupils who did not get into grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary modern is a type of British state secondary school, so it is a school.

clue.text: Best middle-distance runner circling base

indicators.note: circling means going all round, so the runner surrounds the base letter

blocks.note: Steve Cram was a British world-record miler of the 1980s
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: The best middle-distance runner laps round to base.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream is the finest part of something, so it means the best.

clue.text: New and deadly female missed in old province

indicators.note: something missed is left out, so the letter for female is dropped

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
fatal means deadly
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A deadly new female is missing in an old colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994, now part of KwaZulu-Natal.

clue.text: First thirteen letters put with small, small things

blocks.note: the first thirteen letters of the alphabet run A to M
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: The first half of the alphabet is set with small items.
explanation.walkthrough: A TO M describes the alphabet's first thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms are the tiny basic units of matter, the classic small things.

clue.text: Lord's club stocking MDMA: a place attracting many

indicators.note: a shop stocking an item keeps it inside, so the club holds the drug

blocks.note: the Marylebone Cricket Club is based at Lord's, the London cricket ground
MDMA is ecstasy, known as E
taken as written

explanation.surface: A London club stocks ecstasy, and so draws a big crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A mecca, after the holy city that pilgrims visit, is any place that draws many visitors.

clue.text: Forming concepts in hide at Iona

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words, running across them

blocks.note: found running through the three words after the h

explanation.surface: Someone forms ideas while hiding away on Iona, a remote Scottish island known for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideation is the mental process of forming ideas, a noun matching the gerund phrase.

clue.text: Film maker turned up with hawk-headed god

blocks.note: to turn up is to arrive, so came
Ra, the Egyptian sun god, is shown with a falcon's head

explanation.surface: A filmmaker arrives with an Egyptian god in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' tempts a reversal, but in an across clue it simply means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera is the device that makes film images, a film maker taken literally rather than a director.

clue.text: Unbaptised male defective in head

indicators.note: something defective is faulty or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for head

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A male who was never christened is thought to be defective in the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism traditionally gives a child its name, so one never baptised is without a name.

clue.text: Wealth from positions taken on Roman coin

blocks.note: the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
to set something is to position it

explanation.surface: Wealth comes from positions taken in old Roman money.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'taken on' puts the positions after the coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things of value a person owns, which together make up their wealth.
